original_question: For an infinite Frobenius variety V, let G(V) be the directed tree whose vertices are semigroups in V and whose levels are measured by distance from the root N. Determine whether, for every n, the (n + 1)-st level of G(V) contains more vertices than the n-th level.
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Frobenius Varieties"), unnumbered open question stated after the definition of the tree associated to a Frobenius variety: in the infinite-case, ask whether the associated rooted tree has strictly more vertices at level n+1 than at level n, as a generalization of Bras-Amorós' conjecture.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right section and the right open problem: it uses an infinite Frobenius variety V, the associated rooted tree with root N, levels measured by distance from the root, and the strict comparison between consecutive level sizes.
missing_details: It should say explicitly that V is a Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups, not an arbitrary rooted tree or arbitrary family of semigroups.
To be stand-alone, it should define a numerical semigroup as a submonoid of N with finite complement.
It should define a Frobenius variety: a nonempty family V of numerical semigroups such that S,T in V implies S ∩ T in V, and if S in V with S ≠ N, then S ∪ {F(S)} is also in V.
It should define F(S) as the Frobenius number of S, i.e. the largest integer not in S.
It should define the tree G(V) by its edges/parent-child rule, not only by saying it is the directed tree attached to V.
It should make the quantifier explicit: the comparison is intended for every n ≥ 0 (root at level 0).

To stay paper-faithful, it should note that the unrestricted version for arbitrary Frobenius varieties is already known to be false; the paper singles out the infinite case as the remaining open case.
refined_question: Let V be an infinite Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups, where a numerical semigroup is a submonoid S of N = {0,1,2,...} with finite complement, and where V is a nonempty family of numerical semigroups such that (i) S,T in V implies S ∩ T in V, and (ii) if S in V and S ≠ N, then S ∪ {F(S)} is in V, with F(S) the Frobenius number of S. Let G(V) be the rooted tree with vertex set V, root N, and parent relation given by: T is a child of S exactly when S = T ∪ {F(T)}. Is it true that for every n ≥ 0, the number of vertices of G(V) at level n+1 is strictly larger than the number of vertices at level n?
justification: Your draft is already very close to the paper's intended problem. The paper first defines Frobenius varieties and the associated rooted tree G(V), then immediately states this question as a generalization of Bras-Amorós' conjecture. The important paper-faithful sharpening is that the paper explicitly says the general statement is false for some Frobenius varieties and that the open case is when V is infinite, so the refined question should keep that restriction. Adding the formal definitions of numerical semigroup, Frobenius variety, Frobenius number, and the tree relation makes the question fully stand-alone without broadening it beyond the paper.
